Sixty-one eons from this one, there was one named Vimala, a wheel-turning monarch endowed with the seven treasures and of great military power.

29.

29.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges… the teaching of the Buddha has been done.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā udakadāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, it is said, the Venerable Elder Udakadāyaka spoke these verses.

Udakadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The sixth Apadāna of the Elder Udakadāyaka is finished.

7. Salalamāliyattheraapadānaṃ

7. The Apadāna of the Elder Salalamāliya.

30.

30.

“Kaṇikāraṃva [V 1.0214][P 1.0206] jotantaṃ, nisinnaṃ pabbatantare;

Obhāsentaṃ disā sabbā, siddhatthaṃ narasārathiṃ.

I saw the Buddha Siddhattha, the tamer of men, seated in a mountain pass, shining like a kaṇikāra tree, illuminating all directions.

31.

31.

“Dhanuṃ advejjhaṃ katvāna, usuṃ sannayhahaṃ tadā;

Pupphaṃ savaṇṭaṃ chetvāna, buddhassa abhiropayiṃ.

Having made the bow ready with its string and nocked an arrow, I then shot down a flower with its stalk and offered it to the Buddha.

32.

32.

“Catunnavutito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhiropayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-four aeons ago from this aeon, when I offered that flower, I have known no woeful destination. This is the fruit of an offering to the Buddha.

33.

33.

“Ekapaññāsito kappe, eko āsiṃ jutindharo;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Fifty-one aeons ago from this aeon, I was a wheel-turning monarch named Jutindhara, endowed with the seven treasures and of great power.

34.

34.

“Paṭisambhidā [T 1.0306] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā salalamāliyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Salalamāliya spoke these verses.

Salalamāliyattherassāpadānaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Seventh Apadāna of the Elder Salalamāliya.

8. Koraṇḍapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ

8. The Apadāna of the Elder Koraṇḍapupphiya.

35.

35.

“Akkantañca [M 1.0231] padaṃ disvā, cakkālaṅkārabhūsitaṃ;

Padenānupadaṃ yanto, vipassissa mahesino.

Seeing the footprint of the great sage Vipassī, trodden upon and adorned with the ornament of the wheel, I followed in his footsteps.

36.

36.

“Koraṇḍaṃ pupphitaṃ disvā, samūlaṃ pūjitaṃ mayā;

Haṭṭho haṭṭhena cittena, avandiṃ padamuttamaṃ.

Having seen a blooming koraṇḍa flower, I offered it, root and all. Joyful, with a joyful mind, I venerated the supreme footprint.

37.

37.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhipūjayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons ago from this aeon, when I made an offering of that flower, I have known no woeful destination. This is the fruit of an offering to the Buddha.

38.

38.

“Sattapaññāsakappamhi, eko vītamalo ahuṃ;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

In the fifty-seventh aeon from this one, I was a wheel-turning monarch named Vītamala, endowed with the seven treasures and of great power.

39.

39.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ [V 1.0215] sudaṃ āyasmā koraṇḍapupphiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Koraṇḍapupphiya spoke these verses.

Koraṇḍapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Eighth Apadāna of the Elder Koraṇḍapupphiya.

9. Ādhāradāyakattheraapadānaṃ

9. The Apadāna of the Elder Ādhāradāyaka.

40.

40.

“Ādhārakaṃ [T 1.0307][P 1.0207] mayā dinnaṃ, sikhino lokabandhuno;

Dhāremi pathaviṃ sabbaṃ, kevalaṃ vasudhaṃ imaṃ.

A bowl-stand was given by me to Sikhī, the Kinsman of the World; I uphold this entire earth, this whole treasure-bearing land.

41.

41.

“Kilesā jhāpitā mayhaṃ, bhavā sabbe samūhatā;

Dhāremi antimaṃ dehaṃ, sammāsambuddhasāsane.

My defilements are burnt up, all states of existence are uprooted; I bear this final body in the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One.

42.

42.

“Sattavīse ito kappe, ahesuṃ caturo janā;

Samantavaraṇā nāma, cakkavattī mahabbalā.

Twenty-seven aeons ago from this aeon, there were four wheel-turning monarchs of great power, named Samantavaraṇa.

43.

43.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā ādhāradāyako pariyādāniyo (ka.) thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Ādhāradāyaka spoke these verses.

Ādhāradāyakattherassāpadānaṃ navamaṃ.

The Ninth Apadāna of the Elder Ādhāradāyaka.

10. Pāpanivāriyattheraapadānaṃ

10. The Apadāna of the Elder Pāpanivāriya.

44.

44.

“Tissassa [M 1.0232] tu bhagavato, devadevassa tādino;

Ekacchattaṃ mayā dinnaṃ, vippasannena cetasā.

To the Blessed One Tissa, the god of gods, the steadfast one, a single umbrella was given by me with a serene mind.

45.

45.

“Nivutaṃ hoti me pāpaṃ, kusalassupasampadā;

Ākāse chattaṃ dhārenti, pubbakammassidaṃ phalaṃ.

Through the accomplishment of merit, evil is obstructed for me. An umbrella is held for me in the sky; this is the fruit of a past deed.

46.

46.

“Carimaṃ [T 1.0308] vattate mayhaṃ, bhavā sabbe samūhatā;

Dhāremi antimaṃ dehaṃ, sammāsambuddhasāsane.

This is my final existence; all states of being have been uprooted. I bear this final body in the dispensation of the Perfectly Enlightened Buddha.

47.

47.

“Dvenavute ito kappe, yaṃ chattamadadiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, chattadānassidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-two aeons ago from this aeon, when I gave that umbrella, I have known no woeful destination. This is the fruit of the gift of an umbrella.

48.

48.

“Dvesattatimhito kappe, aṭṭhāsiṃsu janādhipā;

Mahānidānanāmena, rājāno cakkavattino.

Seventy-two aeons ago from this aeon, there were eight lords of men, wheel-turning kings by the name of Mahānidāna.

49.

49.

“Paṭisambhidā [V 1.0216] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā pāpanivāriyo vātātapanivāriyo (sī.) thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti;

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled. Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Pāpanivāriya spoke these verses.

Pāpanivāriyattherassāpadānaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth Apadāna of the Elder Pāpanivāriya is finished.

Kaṇikārapupphiyavaggo ekavīsatimo.

The Kaṇikārapupphiya Chapter, the twenty-first.

Tassuddānaṃ [P 1.0208] –

The summary:

Kaṇikāro minelañca, kiṅkaṇi taraṇena ca;

Nigguṇḍipupphī dakado, salalo ca kuraṇḍako;

Ādhārako pāpavārī, aṭṭhatālīsa gāthakāti.

Kaṇikāra, Minela, Kiṅkaṇi, and Taraṇīya, Nigguṇḍipupphī, Udakadāyaka, Salalamāliya, Koraṇḍapupphiya, Ādhāradāyaka, and Pāpanivāriya—the verses are forty-eight in total.

22. Hatthivaggo

22. The Elephant Chapter.

1. Hatthidāyakattheraapadānaṃ

1. The Apadāna of the Elder Hatthidāyaka.

1.

1.

“Siddhatthassa [T 1.0309][M 1.0233][V 1.0217] bhagavato, dvipadindassa tādino;

Nāgaseṭṭho mayā dinno, īsādanto urūḷhavā.

To the Blessed One Siddhattha, the lord of bipeds, the steadfast one, a supreme elephant was given by me, one with tusks like a chariot-pole and able to bear a burden.

2.

2.

“Uttamatthaṃ anubhomi, santipadamanuttaraṃ;

Nāgadānaṃ aggadānaṃ (sī. ka.) mayā dinnaṃ, sabbalokahitesino.

I experience the supreme goal, the unsurpassed state of peace. The gift of an elephant was given by me to the one who seeks the welfare of the entire world.

3.

3.

“Catunnavutito kappe, yaṃ nāga dāna (sī. ka.) madadiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, nāgadānassidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-four aeons ago from this aeon, when I gave that elephant, I have known no woeful destination. This is the fruit of the gift of an elephant.

4.

4.

“Aṭṭhasattatikappamhi, soḷasāsiṃsu khattiyā;

Samantapāsādikā nāma, cakkavattī mahabbalā.

In the seventy-eighth aeon from this one, there were sixteen nobles named Samantapāsādika, wheel-turning monarchs of great power.

5.

5.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso, vimokkhāpi ca aṭṭhime;

Chaḷabhiññā sacchikatā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, and these eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā hatthidāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Hatthidāyaka spoke these verses.

Hatthidāyakattherassāpadānaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first Apadāna of the Elder Hatthidāyaka is concluded.

2. Pānadhidāyakattheraapadānaṃ

2. The Apadāna of the Elder Pānadhidāyaka

6.

6.

“Āraññikassa isino, cirarattatapassino jhāyino, mettacittatapassino (syā.);

Buddhassa dhammassa (syā. ka.) bhāvitattassa, adāsiṃ pānadhiṃ ahaṃ.

To the forest-dwelling sage, a long-time ascetic, one who had cultivated the Dhamma, I gave a pair of sandals.

7.

7.

“Tena [T 1.0310] kammena dvipadinda, lokajeṭṭha narāsabha;

Dibbayānaṃ sabbaṃ yānaṃ (sī.) anubhomi, pubbakammassidaṃ phalaṃ.

By that deed, O lord of bipeds, eldest in the world, bull among men, I experience a divine vehicle; this is the fruit of a previous good deed.

8.

8.

“Catunnavute [P 1.0209] ito kappe, yaṃ kammamakariṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, pānadhissa idaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-four aeons ago from this one, when I performed that deed, I have not known a woeful state; this is the fruit of the gift of sandals.

9.

9.

“Sattasattatito [M 1.0234][V 1.0218] kappe, aṭṭha āsiṃsu khattiyā;

Suyānā nāma nāmena, cakkavattī mahabbalā.

Seventy-seven aeons ago from this one, there were eight khattiyas by the name of Suyāna, wheel-turning monarchs of great power.

10.

10.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six direct knowledges have been realized; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā pānadhidāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the venerable Elder Pānadhidāyaka recited these verses.

Pānadhidāyakattherassāpadānaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second Apadāna of the Elder who gave sandals is concluded.

3. Saccasaññakattheraapadānaṃ

3. The Apadāna of the Elder Saccasaññaka

11.

11.

“Vessabhū tamhi samaye, bhikkhusaṅghapurakkhato;

Deseti ariyasaccāni, nibbāpento mahājanaṃ.

At that time, the Lord Vessabhū, surrounded by the assembly of monks, taught the Noble Truths, bringing peace to the great multitude.

12.

12.

“Paramakāruññapattomhi, samitiṃ agamāsahaṃ;

Sohaṃ nisinnako santo, dhammamassosi satthuno.

I had become most pitiable; I went to the assembly. And so, being seated, I heard the Dhamma of the Teacher.

13.

13.

“Tassāhaṃ dhammaṃ sutvāna, devalokaṃ agacchahaṃ;

Tiṃsakappāni devesu, avasiṃ tatthahaṃ pure.

Having heard his Dhamma, I went to the world of the devas. For thirty aeons in the past, I dwelt there among the devas.

14.

14.

“Ekattiṃse [T 1.0311] ito kappe, yaṃ saññamalabhiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, saccasaññāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

In the thirty-first aeon from this one, when I gained that perception, since then I have not known a woeful state. This is the fruit of the perception of the Truths.

15.

15.

“Chabbīsamhi ito kappe, eko āsiṃ janādhipo;

Ekaphusitanāmena, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

In the twenty-sixth aeon from this one, I was once a ruler of men, a wheel-turning monarch of great strength, by the name of Ekaphusita.

16.

16.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six direct knowledges have been realized; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā saccasaññako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the venerable Elder Saccasaññaka spoke these verses.

Saccasaññakattherassāpadānaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third Apadāna of the Elder Saccasaññaka is concluded.

4. Ekasaññakattheraapadānaṃ

4. The Apadāna of the Elder Ekasaññaka

17.

17.

“Dumagge paṃsukūlikaṃ paṃsukūlakaṃ (?), laggaṃ disvāna satthuno;

Añjaliṃ paggahetvāna, paṃsukūlaṃ avandahaṃ.

Seeing the Teacher's dust-heap robe caught on a treetop, having raised my joined hands in reverence, I venerated that dust-heap robe.

18.

18.

“Ekattiṃse ito kappe, yaṃ saññamalabhiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

In the thirty-first aeon from this one, when I gained that perception, since then I have not known a woeful state. This is the fruit of honoring the Buddha.

19.

19.

“Pañcavīse [M 1.0235][V 1.0219][P 1.0210] ito kappe, eko āsiṃ janādhipo;

Amitābhoti nāmena, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

In the twenty-fifth aeon from this one, I was once a ruler of men, a wheel-turning monarch of great strength, by the name of Amitābha.

20.

20.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six direct knowledges have been realized; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ [T 1.0312] sudaṃ āyasmā ekasaññako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the venerable Elder Ekasaññaka spoke these verses.

Ekasaññakattherassāpadānaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth Apadāna of the Elder Ekasaññaka is concluded.

5. Raṃsisaññakattheraapadānaṃ

5. The Apadāna of the Elder Raṃsisaññaka

21.

21.

“Udentaṃ sataraṃsiṃva, pītaraṃsiṃva sitaraṃsiṃ va (sī. syā.) bhāṇumaṃ;

Byagghūsabhaṃva pavaraṃ, sujātaṃ pabbatantare.

I saw the Lord Sujāta in a mountain pass, like the rising, hundred-rayed sun, luminous with yellow rays, noble like a tiger-bull.

22.

22.

“Buddhassa ānubhāvo so, jalate pabbatantare;

Raṃse raṃsyā (?) cittaṃ pasādetvā, kappaṃ saggamhi modahaṃ.

That power of the Buddha blazes in the mountain pass. Having gladdened my mind in his radiance, I rejoiced in heaven for an aeon.

23.

23.

“Avasesesu kappesu, kusalaṃ caritaṃ mayā;

Tena cittappasādena, buddhānussatiyāpi ca.

In the remaining aeons, wholesome action was performed by me, because of that serenity of mind and also through the recollection of the Buddha.

24.

24.

“Tiṃsakappasahasseto, yaṃ saññamalabhiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhasaññāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Thirty thousand aeons from this one, when I gained that perception, since then I have not known a woeful state. This is the fruit of the perception of the Buddha.

25.

25.

“Sattapaññāsakappamhi, eko āsiṃ janādhipo;

Sujāto nāma nāmena, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

In the fifty-seventh aeon, I was once a ruler of men, a wheel-turning monarch of great strength, known by the name Sujāta.

26.

26.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six direct knowledges have been realized; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā raṃsisaññako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the venerable Elder Raṃsisaññaka spoke these verses.

Raṃsisaññakattherassāpadānaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The fifth Apadāna of the Elder Raṃsisaññaka is concluded.

6. Sandhitattheraapadānaṃ

6. The Apadāna of the Elder Sandhita

27.

27.

“Assatthe [T 1.0313] haritobhāse, saṃvirūḷhamhi pādape;

Ekaṃ buddhagataṃ saññaṃ, alabhiṃhaṃ alabhissaṃ (sī.) patissato.

At the flourishing Assattha tree of greenish hue, I, being mindful, obtained a single perception directed towards the Buddha.

28.

28.

“Ekattiṃse [M 1.0236] ito kappe, yaṃ saññamalabhiṃ tadā;

Tassā saññāya vāhasā, patto me āsavakkhayo.

In the thirty-first aeon from this one, by the power of that perception which I then obtained, I have attained the destruction of the cankers.

29.

29.

“Ito [V 1.0220] terasakappamhi, dhaniṭṭho nāma khattiyo;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Thirteen aeons from this one, I was a khattiya named Dhaniṭṭha, endowed with the seven treasures, a wheel-turning monarch of great power.

30.

30.

“Paṭisambhidā [P 1.0211] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six direct knowledges have been realized; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā sandhito saṇṭhito (sī.) thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the venerable Elder Sandhita spoke these verses.

Sandhitattherassāpadānaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Sixth Apadāna of the Elder Sandhita.

7. Tālavaṇṭadāyakattheraapadānaṃ

7. The Apadāna of the Elder Tālavaṇṭadāyaka

31.

31.

“Tālavaṇṭaṃ mayā dinnaṃ, tissassādiccabandhuno;

Gimhanibbāpanatthāya, pariḷāhopasantiyā.

A palm-leaf fan was given by me to Tissa, the kinsman of the sun, for the purpose of extinguishing the summer heat and for the pacification of burning distress.

32.

32.

“Sannibbāpemi rāgaggiṃ, dosaggiñca taduttariṃ;

Nibbāpemi ca mohaggiṃ, tālavaṇṭassidaṃ phalaṃ.

I extinguish the fire of lust, and likewise the fire of hatred; furthermore, I extinguish the fire of delusion. This is the fruit of the palm-leaf fan.

33.

33.

“Kilesā [T 1.0314] jhāpitā mayhaṃ, bhavā sabbe samūhatā;

Dhāremi antimaṃ dehaṃ, sammāsambuddhasāsane.

My defilements have been burned; all states of existence have been uprooted. I bear my final body in the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One.

34.

34.

“Dvenavute ito kappe, yaṃ kammamakariṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, tālavaṇṭassidaṃ phalaṃ.

In the ninety-second aeon from this one, for the kamma I performed then, I have known no woeful state. This is the fruit of the palm-leaf fan.

35.

35.

“Tesaṭṭhimhi ito kappe, mahānāmasanāmako;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Sixty-three aeons from this one, I was a wheel-turning monarch of great power, endowed with the seven treasures, known by the name Mahānāma.

36.

36.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā tālavaṇṭadāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, it is said, the Venerable Elder Tālavaṇṭadāyaka spoke these verses.

Tālavaṇṭadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Seventh Apadāna of the Elder Tālavaṇṭadāyaka.

8. Akkantasaññakattheraapadānaṃ

8. The Apadāna of the Elder Akkantasaññaka

37.

37.

“Kusāṭakaṃ [M 1.0237] gahetvāna, upajjhāyassahaṃ pure;

Mantañca anusikkhāmi, ganthādosassa kaṇḍabhedassa (sī.), gaṇḍabhedassa (syā.) pattiyā.

Formerly, having taken a contemptible garment, I was with my preceptor; I was also studying the sacred texts for the sake of attaining faultlessness in the scriptures.

38.

38.

“Addasaṃ virajaṃ buddhaṃ, āhutīnaṃ paṭiggahaṃ;

Usabhaṃ pavaraṃ aggaṃ, tissaṃ buddhaṃ gaṇuttamaṃ gajuttamaṃ (syā.).

I saw the dust-free Buddha, worthy of offerings, a bull among men, the noble, the supreme, the Buddha Tissa, the best of the multitude.

39.

39.

“Kusāṭakaṃ [V 1.0221] pattharitaṃ, akkamantaṃ naruttamaṃ;

Samuggataṃ mahāvīraṃ, lokajeṭṭhaṃ narāsabhaṃ.

The contemptible garment was spread out for the supreme man to tread upon—the eminent great hero, the world's chief, the bull among men.

40.

40.

“Disvā [T 1.0315][P 1.0212] taṃ lokapajjotaṃ, vimalaṃ candasannibhaṃ;

Avandiṃ satthuno pāde, vippasannena cetasā.

Having seen that light of the world, stainless and like unto the moon, with a serene mind, I paid homage to the Teacher's feet.

41.

41.

“Catunnavutito kappe, yaṃ adāsiṃ kusāṭakaṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, kusāṭakassidaṃ phalaṃ.

In the ninety-fourth aeon from this one, for the contemptible garment I gave, I have known no woeful state. This is the fruit of the contemptible garment.

42.

42.

“Sattatiṃse ito kappe, eko āsiṃ janādhipo;

Sunando nāma nāmena, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Thirty-seven aeons from this one, I was a sole ruler of men, Sunanda by name, a wheel-turning monarch of great power.

43.

43.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā akkantasaññako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti;

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled. Thus, it is said, the Venerable Elder Akkantasaññaka spoke these verses.

Akkantasaññakattherassāpadānaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Eighth Apadāna of the Elder Akkantasaññaka.

9. Sappidāyakattheraapadānaṃ

9. The Apadāna of the Elder Sappidāyaka

44.

44.

“Nisinno pāsādavare, nārīgaṇapurakkhato;

Byādhitaṃ samaṇaṃ disvā, abhināmesahaṃ gharaṃ.

Seated in an excellent palace, surrounded by a retinue of women, having seen an afflicted monk, I invited him to my home.

45.

45.

“Upaviṭṭhaṃ mahāvīraṃ, devadevaṃ narāsabhaṃ;

Sappitelaṃ mayā dinnaṃ, siddhatthassa mahesino.

To the great hero who was seated, the god beyond gods, the bull among men, to the great sage Siddhattha, I gave ghee-oil.

46.

46.

“Passaddhadarathaṃ disvā, vippasannamukhindriyaṃ;

Vanditvā satthuno pāde, anusaṃsāvayiṃ pure.

Having seen him with anxiety stilled, with a serene face and faculties, I worshipped the Teacher's feet and praised him in his presence.

47.

47.

“Disvā [T 1.0316][M 1.0238] maṃ suppasannattaṃ suppasannantaṃ (syā. ka.) suppasannacittanti attho, iddhiyā pāramiṅgato;

Nabhaṃ abbhuggamī dhīro, haṃsarājāva ambare.

Seeing me so very serene, the wise one, who had reached the further shore, rose into the sky by psychic power, like a swan-king in the heavens.

48.

48.

“Catunnavutito kappe, yaṃ dānamadadiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, sappitelassidaṃ phalaṃ.

In the ninety-fourth aeon from this one, for the gift that I gave then, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of the ghee-oil.

49.

49.

“Ito sattarase kappe, jutideva dutideva (syā.), tutideva (ka.) sanāmako;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Seventeen aeons from this one, I was a wheel-turning monarch of great strength, endowed with the seven treasures, by the name of Jutideva.

50.

50.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā sappidāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the Venerable Elder Sappidāyaka spoke these verses.

Sappidāyakattherassāpadānaṃ navamaṃ.

The Ninth Apadāna of the Elder Sappidāyaka.

10. Pāpanivāriyattheraapadānaṃ

10. The Apadāna of the Elder Pāpanivāriya

51.

51.

“Piyadassissa [V 1.0222] bhagavato, caṅkamaṃ sodhitaṃ mayā;

Naḷakehi paṭicchannaṃ, vātātapanivāraṇaṃ.

I cleared the walkway for the Blessed One, Piyadassī, which was covered with reeds and gave protection from wind and sun.

52.

52.

“Pāpaṃ vivajjanatthāya, kusalassupasampadā;

Kilesānaṃ pahānāya, padahiṃ satthu sāsane.

For the sake of avoiding evil, for the accomplishment of the wholesome, and for the abandoning of defilements, I strove in the Teacher's Dispensation.

53.

53.

“Ito [P 1.0213] ekādase kappe, aggidevoti vissuto;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Eleven aeons from this one, I was a wheel-turning monarch of great strength, endowed with the seven treasures, renowned as Aggideva.

54.

54.

“Paṭisambhidā [T 1.0317] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā pāpanivāriyo vātātapanivāriyo (?) thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the Venerable Elder Pāpanivāriya spoke these verses.

Pāpanivāriyattherassāpadānaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Tenth Apadāna of the Elder Pāpanivāriya.

Hatthivaggo bāvīsatimo.

The Hatthi Chapter, the twenty-second.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Hatthi pānadhi saccañca, ekasaññi ca raṃsiko;

Sandhito tālavaṇṭañca, tathā akkantasaññako;

Sappi pāpanivārī ca, catuppaññāsa gāthakāti.

Hatthi, Pānadhi, and Sacca, Ekasaññi and Raṃsika, Sandhita and Tālavaṇṭa, also Akkantasaññaka, Sappi and Pāpanivārī; the verses are fifty-four.

23. Ālambaṇadāyakavaggo

23. The Ālambaṇadāyaka Chapter

1. Ālambaṇadāyakattheraapadānaṃ

1. The Apadāna of the Elder Ālambaṇadāyaka

1.

1.

“Atthadassissa [T 1.0318][M 1.0239][V 1.0223] bhagavato, lokajeṭṭhassa tādino;

Ālambaṇaṃ mayā dinnaṃ, dvipadindassa tādino.

To the Blessed One Atthadassī, chief of the world, the steadfast one, a support was given by me, to the lord of bipeds, the steadfast one.

2.

2.

“Dharaṇiṃ paṭipajjāmi, vipulaṃ sāgarapparaṃ;

Pāṇesu ca issariyaṃ, vattemi vasudhāya ca.

I rule the vast, ocean-bounded earth; I exercise sovereignty over beings and over the land.

3.

3.

“Kilesā jhāpitā mayhaṃ, bhavā sabbe samūhatā;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ.

My defilements are burned up, all states of existence are uprooted; the three knowledges have been attained, the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

4.

4.

“Ito dvesaṭṭhikappamhi, tayo āsiṃsu khattiyā;

Ekāpassitanāmā te, cakkavattī mahabbalā.

Sixty-two aeons from this one, I was three times a khattiya; they were mighty wheel-turning monarchs named Ekāpassita.

5.

5.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso, vimokkhāpi ca aṭṭhime;

Chaḷabhiññā sacchikatā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, and these eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized; the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā ālambaṇadāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Ālambaṇadāyaka spoke these verses.

Ālambaṇadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The First Apadāna of the Elder Ālambaṇadāyaka.

2. Ajinadāyakattheraapadānaṃ

2. The Apadāna of the Elder Ajinadāyaka

6.

6.

“Ekattiṃse ito kappe, gaṇasatthārako ahaṃ;

Addasaṃ virajaṃ buddhaṃ, āhutīnaṃ paṭiggahaṃ.

Thirty-one aeons from this one, I was a teacher of a group. I saw the dust-free Buddha, worthy of receiving offerings.

7.

7.

“Cammakhaṇḍaṃ [T 1.0319] mayā dinnaṃ, sikhino lokabandhuno;

Tena kammena dvipadinda, lokajeṭṭha narāsabha.

I gave a piece of hide to Sikhī, the Kinsman of the World. By that deed—O master of bipeds, chief of the world, bull among men—

8.

8.

“Sampattiṃ [P 1.0214] anubhotvāna, kilese jhāpayiṃ ahaṃ;

Dhāremi antimaṃ dehaṃ, sammāsambuddhasāsane.

having enjoyed prosperity, I have burned up the defilements. I bear my final body in the Dispensation of the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

9.

9.

“Ekattiṃse [V 1.0224] ito kappe, ajinaṃ yaṃ adāsahaṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, ajinassa idaṃ phalaṃ.

Thirty-one aeons from this one, when I gave that hide, I have not known a woeful state since then. This is the fruit of giving the hide.

10.

10.

“Ito pañcamake kappe, rājā āsiṃ sudāyako;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

In the fifth aeon from this one, I was a king named Sudāyaka, endowed with the seven treasures, a wheel-turning monarch of great strength.

11.

11.

“Paṭisambhidā [M 1.0240] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, and these eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized; the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā ajinadāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Ajinadāyaka spoke these verses.

Ajinadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Second Apadāna of the Elder Ajinadāyaka.

3. Dverataniyattheraapadānaṃ

3. The Apadāna of the Elder Dverataniya

12.

12.

“Migaluddo pure āsiṃ, araññe kānane ahaṃ;

Addasaṃ virajaṃ buddhaṃ, āhutīnaṃ paṭiggahaṃ.

Formerly, I was a deer-hunter in the wilderness, in the forest. I saw the dust-free Buddha, worthy of receiving offerings.

13.

13.

“Maṃsapesi mayā dinnā, vipassissa mahesino;

Sadevakasmiṃ lokasmiṃ, issaraṃ kārayāmahaṃ.

A piece of meat was given by me to the great seeker, Vipassī. In the world with its devas, I exercise lordship.

14.

14.

“Iminā [T 1.0320] maṃsadānena, ratanaṃ nibbattate mama;

Duveme ratanā loke, diṭṭhadhammassa pattiyā.

Through this gift of meat, treasure arises for me. These two treasures are mine in the world for the attainment of welfare in this present life.

15.

15.

“Tehaṃ sabbe anubhomi, maṃsadānassa sattiyā;

Gattañca mudukaṃ mayhaṃ, paññā nipuṇavedanī.

I enjoy all of them through the power of the gift of meat. My body is soft, and I experience subtle wisdom.

16.

16.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ maṃsamadadiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, maṃsadānassidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons ago, when I gave that piece of meat, I have not known a woeful state since then. This is the fruit of the gift of meat.

17.

17.

“Ito catutthake kappe, eko āsiṃ janādhipo;

Mahārohitanāmo so, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

In the fourth aeon from this one, I was a ruler of people named Mahārohita, a wheel-turning monarch of great strength.

18.

18.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, and these eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized; the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā dverataniyo dvirataniyo (sī.) thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Dverataniya spoke these verses.

Dverataniyattherassāpadānaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Third Apadāna of the Elder Dverataniya.

Dasamaṃ bhāṇavāraṃ.

The Tenth Recitation Section.

4. Ārakkhadāyakattheraapadānaṃ

4. The Apadāna of the Elder Ārakkhadāyaka

19.

19.

“Siddhatthassa [V 1.0225] bhagavato, vedi kārāpitā vedikā kāritā (syā.) mayā;

Ārakkho ca mayā dinno, sugatassa mahesino.

I had a railing made for the Blessed One, Siddhattha. And protection was given by me to the Well-Gone One, the great seeker.

20.

20.

“Tena [M 1.0241] kammavisesena, na passiṃ bhayabheravaṃ;

Kuhiñci upapannassa, tāso mayhaṃ na vijjati.

Because of that special deed, I have not seen fear and terror. For me, reborn anywhere at all, there is no fright.

21.

21.

“Catunnavutito [T 1.0321][P 1.0215] kappe, yaṃ vediṃ kārayiṃ pure;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, vedikāya idaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-four aeons ago, when I had that railing made, I have not known a woeful state since then. This is the fruit of the railing.

22.

22.

“Ito chaṭṭhamhi kappamhi, apassenasanāmako;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

In the sixth aeon from this one, I was a wheel-turning monarch of great strength named Apassena, endowed with the seven treasures.

23.

23.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, and these eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized; the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā ārakkhadāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Ārakkhadāyaka spoke these verses.

Ārakkhadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Fourth Apadāna of the Elder Ārakkhadāyaka.

5. Abyādhikattheraapadānaṃ

5. The Apadāna of the Elder Abyādhika

24.

24.

“Vipassissa bhagavato, aggisālaṃ adāsahaṃ;

Byādhikānañca āvāsaṃ, uṇhodakapaṭiggahaṃ.

To the Blessed One Vipassī, I gave a fire-hall; and to the sick, I gave a dwelling and a pot for receiving warm water.

25.

25.

“Tena kammenayaṃ mayhaṃ, attabhāvo sunimmito;

Byādhāhaṃ nābhijānāmi, puññakammassidaṃ phalaṃ.

By that deed, this existence of mine is well-created. I have never known illness; this is the fruit of meritorious deeds.

26.

26.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ sālamadadiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, aggisālāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons ago, when I gave that hall, I have not known a woeful state since then. This is the fruit of the fire-hall.

27.

27.

“Ito ca sattame kappe, ekosiṃ aparājito eko āsiṃ narādhipo (syā.);

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Seven aeons from this one, I was a single universal monarch named Aparājita, endowed with the seven treasures and of great strength.

28.

28.

“Paṭisambhidā [T 1.0322][P 1.0216] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā abyādhiko thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the venerable Elder Abyādhika spoke these verses.

Abyādhikattherassāpadānaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The fifth Apadāna of the Elder Abyādhika.

6. Aṅkolapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ

6. The Apadāna of the Elder Aṅkolapupphiya.

29.

29.

“Nārado [M 1.0242][V 1.0226] varado (ka.) iti me nāmaṃ, kassapo iti maṃ vidū;

Addasaṃ samaṇānaggaṃ, vipassiṃ devasakkataṃ.

My name is Nārada; they know me as Kassapa. I saw Vipassī, foremost among ascetics, honored by devas.

30.

30.

“Anubyañjanadharaṃ buddhaṃ, āhutīnaṃ paṭiggahaṃ;

Aṅkolapupphaṃ vakulapupphaṃ (syā.), bakolapupphaṃ (ka.) paggayha, buddhassa abhiropayiṃ.

Having taken up an Aṅkola flower, I offered it to the Buddha, the bearer of the minor characteristics, the one worthy of offerings.

31.

31.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhipūjayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons ago, when I offered that flower in worship, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.

32.

32.

“Catusattatito kappe, romaso nāma khattiyo;

Āmukkamālābharaṇo, sayoggabalavāhano.

Seventy-four aeons from this one, I was a khattiya named Romasa, adorned with garlands and ornaments, possessing conveyances, troops, and vehicles.

33.

33.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā aṅkolapupphiyo vakulapupphiyo (syā.), bakolapupphiyo (ka.) thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the venerable Elder Aṅkolapupphiya spoke these verses.

Aṅkolapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The sixth Apadāna of the Elder Aṅkolapupphiya.

7. Sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ

7. The Apadāna of the Elder Sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiya.

34.

34.

“Uyyānabhūmiṃ [T 1.0323] niyyanto, addasaṃ lokanāyakaṃ;

Vaṭaṃsakaṃ gahetvāna, sovaṇṇaṃ sādhunimmitaṃ.

While going out to the park-land, I saw the Leader of the World; having taken a beautifully crafted golden head-ornament,

35.

35.

“Sīghaṃ tato samāruyha, hatthikkhandhagato ahaṃ;

Buddhassa abhiropesiṃ, sikhino lokabandhuno.

I, who was on the back of an elephant, quickly riding up from there, made an offering to the Buddha Sikhī, the kinsman of the world.

36.

36.

“Ekattiṃse ito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhiropayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, pupphapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Thirty-one aeons from this one, when I offered up that flower, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of that flower offering.

37.

37.

“Sattavīse ito kappe, eko āsiṃ janādhipo;

Mahāpatāpanāmena, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Twenty-seven aeons from this one, I was a single ruler of men, a universal monarch of great strength, by the name of Mahāpatāpa.

38.

38.

“Paṭisambhidā [M 1.0243] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the venerable Elder Sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiya spoke these verses.

Sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiyattherassāpadānaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh Apadāna of the Elder Sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiya.

8. Miñjavaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ

8. The Apadāna of the Elder Miñjavaṭaṃsakiya.

39.

39.

“Nibbute [V 1.0227] lokanāthamhi, sikhimhi vadataṃ vare;

Vaṭaṃsakehi ākiṇṇaṃ, bodhipūjaṃ akāsahaṃ.

When Sikhī, the Lord of the World, the foremost among speakers, had attained Parinibbāna, I performed an offering to the Bodhi tree, strewn with head-ornaments.

40.

40.

“Ekattiṃse [T 1.0324] ito kappe, yaṃ pūjamakariṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, bodhipūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Thirty-one aeons from this one, for the offering I made at that time, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of offering to the Bodhi tree.

41.

41.

“Ito chabbīsatikappe, ahuṃ meghabbhanāmako;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Twenty-six aeons from this one, I was one named Meghabbha, a universal monarch of great strength, endowed with the seven treasures.

42.

42.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā miñjavaṭaṃsakiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the venerable Elder Miñjavaṭaṃsakiya spoke these verses.

Miñjavaṭaṃsakiyattherassāpadānaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The eighth Apadāna of the Elder Miñjavaṭaṃsakiya.

9. Sukatāveḷiyattheraapadānaṃ

9. The Apadāna of the Elder Sukatāveḷiya.

43.

43.

“Asito [P 1.0217] nāma nāmena, mālākāro ahaṃ ahuṃ (?) tadā;

Āveḷaṃ paggahetvāna, rañño dātuṃ vajāmahaṃ.

At that time, I was a garland-maker named Asita. Having taken up a floral garland, I was going to give it to the king.

44.

44.

“Asampattomhi asampattamhi (sī.), asampattova (?) rājānaṃ, addasaṃ sikhināyakaṃ;

Haṭṭho haṭṭhena cittena, buddhassa abhiropayiṃ.

Before I reached the king, I saw the leader Sikhī. Joyful, and with a joyful mind, I offered it to the Buddha.

45.

45.

“Ekattiṃse ito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhipūjayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Thirty-one aeons from this one, when I worshipped with that flower, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.

46.

46.

“Pañcavīse [M 1.0244] ito kappe, rājāhosiṃ mahabbalo;

Vebhāro nāma nāmena, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Twenty-five aeons from this one, I was a king of great strength, a universal monarch of great might, Vebhāra by name.

47.

47.

“Paṭisambhidā [T 1.0325] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā sukatāveḷiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the venerable Elder Sukatāveḷiya spoke these verses.

Sukatāveḷiyattherassāpadānaṃ navamaṃ.

The ninth Apadāna of the Elder Sukatāveḷiya.

10. Ekavandaniyattheraapadānaṃ

10. The Apadāna of the Elder Ekavandaniya.

48.

48.

“Usabhaṃ [V 1.0228] pavaraṃ vīraṃ, vessabhuṃ vijitāvinaṃ;

Pasannacitto sumano, buddhaseṭṭhamavandahaṃ.

With a confident and joyful mind, I venerated the supreme Buddha Vessabhū—the bull, the excellent one, the hero, the conqueror.

49.

49.

“Ekattiṃse ito kappe, yaṃ kammamakariṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, vandanāya idaṃ phalaṃ.

Thirty-one aeons from this one, for the kamma that I performed at that time, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of that veneration.

50.

50.

“Catuvīsatikappamhi, vikatānandanāmako;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

In the twenty-fourth aeon, I was a universal monarch of great strength named Vikatānanda, endowed with the seven treasures.

51.

51.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā ekavandaniyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus the Venerable Elder Ekavandaniya spoke these verses.

Ekavandaniyattherassāpadānaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Tenth Apadāna of the Elder Ekavandaniya.

Ālambaṇadāyakavaggo tevīsatimo.

The Twenty-third Chapter: The Giver of a Support.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Ālambaṇañca [T 1.0326] ajinaṃ, maṃsadārakkhadāyako;

Abyādhi aṅkolaṃ vakulaṃ (syā.), bakuḷaṃ (ka.) soṇṇaṃ, miñjaāveḷavandanaṃ;

Pañcapaññāsa gāthāyo, gaṇitā atthadassibhi.

Ālambaṇa and Ajina, Maṃsada, Ārakkhadāyaka; Abyādhi, Aṅkola, Soṇṇa, Miñja, Āveḷa, and Vandana. Fifty-five verses have been counted by those who see the meaning.

24. Udakāsanavaggo

24. The Water-Seat Chapter

1. Udakāsanadāyakattheraapadānaṃ

1. The Apadāna of the Elder Who Gave a Water-Seat

1.

1.

“Ārāmadvārā [M 1.0245][V 1.0229][P 1.0218] nikkhamma, phalakaṃ santhariṃ ahaṃ;

Udakañca upaṭṭhāsiṃ, uttamatthassa pattiyā.

Having gone out from the monastery gate for the attainment of the highest goal, I spread out a plank and also set out water.

2.

2.

“Ekattiṃse ito kappe, yaṃ kammamakariṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, āsane codake phalaṃ.

In the thirty-first aeon from this one, for the deed I did then, I have not known a woeful state; this is the fruit of the seat and the water.

3.

3.

“Ito pannarase kappe, abhisāmasamavhayo;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

In the fifteenth aeon from this one, I was a wheel-turning monarch of great strength named Abhisāmasama, endowed with the seven treasures.

4.

4.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso, vimokkhāpi ca aṭṭhime;

Chaḷabhiññā sacchikatā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, and these eight liberations, and the six direct knowledges have been realized; the Buddha's teaching has been fulfilled.

14.

17.

19.

“Ekanavutito kappe, kāresiṃ vedikaṃ ahaṃ;

21.

22.

27.

27.

Udakāsanavaggo catuvīsatimo.

The Twenty-fourth Chapter: The Water Seat.

Tassuddānaṃ [P 1.0222] –

The summary:

Udakāsanabhājanaṃ, sālapupphī kilañjako;

Vedikā vaṇṇakāro ca, piyālaambayāgado;

Jagatī vāsidātā ca, gāthā tiṃsa ca aṭṭha ca.

Udakāsana, Bhājana, Sālapupphiya, Kilañjaka, Vedikā, Vaṇṇakāra, Piyāla, Ambayāgadāyaka, Jagatidāyaka, and Vāsidāyaka. And there are thirty-eight verses.

25. Tuvaradāyakavaggo

25. The Chapter of the Giver of Tuvara

1. Tuvaradāyakattheraapadānaṃ

1. The Apadāna of the Elder Tuvaradāyaka

1.

1.

“Migaluddo [T 1.0334][M 1.0250][V 1.0234] pure āsiṃ, araññe kānane ahaṃ;

Formerly, I was a hunter in the wilderness, in the great forest. Having taken tuvara seeds and filled a container, I gave them to the Saṅgha.

2.

2.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ dānamadadiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, tuvarassa idaṃ phalaṃ.

3.

3.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso, vimokkhāpi ca aṭṭhime;

6.

“Dvenavute ito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhipūjayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

10.

14.

Ekā dhātu mayā laddhā, dvipadindassa tādino.

When the World-Protector, Siddhattha, the supreme among men, had passed into Nibbāna, one relic of the lord of bipeds, the steadfast one, was obtained by me.

24.

24.

“Tāhaṃ [T 1.0338] dhātuṃ gahetvāna, buddhassādiccabandhuno;

Pañcavasse paricariṃ, tiṭṭhantaṃva naruttamaṃ.

I, having taken that relic of the Buddha, kinsman of the sun, attended to it for five years as though attending to the supreme man standing there.

25.

25.

“Catunnavutito [M 1.0253] kappe, yaṃ dhātuṃ pūjayiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, dhātupaṭṭhahane phalaṃ.

In the ninety-fourth aeon from this one, when I worshipped that relic, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of attending to the relic.

26.

26.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges… the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā dhātupūjako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Dhātupūjaka spoke these verses.

Dhātupūjakattherassāpadānaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh Apadāna concerning the Elder Dhātupūjaka is concluded.

8. Sattalipupphapūjakattheraapadānaṃ

8. The Apadāna of the Elder Sattalipupphapūjaka

27.

27.

“Satta [V 1.0237] sattalipupphāni, sīse katvānahaṃ tadā;

Buddhassa abhiropesiṃ, vessabhumhi naruttame vibhattivipallāso cintetabbo.

At that time, having placed seven sattali flowers on my head, I offered them to the Buddha Vessabhū, the supreme among men.

28.

28.

“Ekattiṃse ito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhipūjayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

In the thirty-first aeon from this one, when I worshipped with that flower, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.

29.

29.

“Paṭisambhidā [P 1.0225] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges… the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā sattalipupphapūjako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Sattalipupphapūjaka Thera spoke these verses.

Sattalipupphapūjakattherassāpadānaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The eighth Apadāna concerning the Elder Sattalipupphapūjaka is concluded.

9. Bimbijāliyattheraapadānaṃ

9. The Apadāna of the Elder Bimbijāliya

30.

30.

“Padumuttaro [T 1.0339] nāma jino, sayambhū aggapuggalo;

Catusaccaṃ pakāseti, dīpeti amataṃ padaṃ.

The Conqueror named Padumuttara, the Self-arisen One, the foremost person, made known the four truths and illuminated the deathless state.

31.

31.

“Bimbijālakapupphāni bimbajālakapupphāni (ka.), puthu katvānahaṃ tadā;

Buddhassa abhiropesiṃ, dvipadindassa tādino.

At that time, having made a profusion of bimbijālaka flowers, I offered them to the Buddha, the lord of bipeds, the steadfast one.

32.

32.

“Aṭṭhasaṭṭhimhito kappe, caturo kiñjakesarā;

Sattaratanasampannā, cakkavattī mahabbalā.

In the sixty-eighth aeon from this one, there were four wheel-turning monarchs named Kiñjakesara, endowed with the seven treasures and of great might.

33.

33.

“Paṭisambhidā [M 1.0254] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges… the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā bimbijāliyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Bimbijāliya Thera spoke these verses.

Bimbijāliyattherassāpadānaṃ navamaṃ.

The ninth Apadāna concerning the Elder Bimbijāliya is concluded.

10. Uddālakadāyakattheraapadānaṃ

10. The Apadāna of the Elder Uddālakadāyaka

34.

34.

“Kakudho nāma nāmena, sayambhū aparājito;

Pavanā nikkhamitvāna, anuppatto mahānadiṃ.

The Unconquered One, the Self-Become, named Kakudha, having departed from the forest, arrived at the great river.

35.

35.

“Uddālakaṃ [V 1.0238] gahetvāna, sayambhussa adāsahaṃ;

Saṃyatassujubhūtassa, pasannamānaso ahaṃ.

Having taken an uddālaka flower, I, with a devoted mind, gave it to the Self-Become One, who is restrained and upright.

36.

36.

“Ekattiṃse [T 1.0340] ito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhipūjayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, pupphadānassidaṃ phalaṃ.

In the thirty-first aeon from this one, for that flower with which I worshipped, I have known no woeful state. This is the fruit of a flower-offering.

37.

37.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā uddālakadāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the Venerable Elder Uddālakadāyaka recited these verses.

Uddālakadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth Apadāna concerning the Elder Uddālakadāyaka is concluded.

Tuvaradāyakavaggo pañcavīsatimo.

The Tuvaradāyaka Chapter, the twenty-fifth, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ [P 1.0226] –

The summary:

Tuvaranāganaḷinā, viravī kuṭidhūpako;

Patto dhātusattaliyo, bimbi uddālakena ca;

Sattatiṃsati gāthāyo, gaṇitāyo vibhāvibhi.

Tuvara, Nāga, Naḷi, Viravi, Kuṭidhūmaka, Patta, Dhātu, Sattaḷiya, Bimbaka, and Uddālaka. The verses, as counted by the discerning, are thirty-seven.

26. Thomakavaggo

26. The Thomaka Chapter

1. Thomakattheraapadānaṃ

1. The Apadāna of the Elder Thomaka

1.

1.

“Devaloke [T 1.0341][M 1.0255][V 1.0239] ṭhito santo, vipassissa mahesino;

Dhammaṃ suṇitvā mudito, imaṃ vācaṃ abhāsahaṃ.

While I was in the deva world, I heard the Dhamma of the Great Sage Vipassī. Delighted, I spoke this utterance:

2.

2.

“‘Namo te purisājañña, namo te purisuttama;

Bahujjanaṃ bahuṃ janaṃ (sī.) tārayasi, desento amataṃ padaṃ’.

‘Homage to you, O thoroughbred of men! Homage to you, O supreme among men! Teaching the deathless state, you ferry the great populace across.’

3.

3.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ vācamabhaṇiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, thomanāya idaṃ phalaṃ.

In the ninety-first aeon from this one, for that utterance I spoke then, I have known no woeful state. This is the fruit of praise.

4.

4.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso, vimokkhāpi ca aṭṭhime;

Chaḷabhiññā sacchikatā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, and these eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā thomako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the Venerable Elder Thomaka recited these verses.

Thomakattherassāpadānaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first Apadāna concerning the Elder Thomaka is concluded.

2. Ekāsanadāyakattheraapadānaṃ

2. The Apadāna of the Elder Ekāsanadāyaka

5.

5.

“Vijahitvā devavaṇṇaṃ, sabhariyo idhāgamiṃ;

Adhikāraṃ kattukāmo, buddhaseṭṭhassa sāsane.

Having abandoned the appearance of a deva, I came here with my wife, desiring to undertake a great service in the teaching of the supreme Buddha.

6.

6.

“Devalo nāma nāmena, padumuttarasāvako;

Tassa bhikkhā mayā dinnā, vippasannena cetasā.

There was a disciple of the Buddha Padumuttara, named Devala. To him, alms-food was given by me with a very devoted mind.

7.

7.

“Satasahassito [T 1.0342] kappe, yaṃ kammamakariṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, piṇḍapātassidaṃ phalaṃ.

One hundred thousand aeons ago, for that deed I performed then, I have known no woeful state. This is the fruit of the alms-food offering.

8.

8.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā ekāsanadāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the Venerable Elder Ekāsanadāyaka recited these verses.

Ekāsanadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second Apadāna of the Elder Ekāsanadāyaka is finished.

3. Citakapūjakattheraapadānaṃ

3. The Apadāna of the Elder Citakapūjaka

9.

9.

“Ānando [M 1.0256][V 1.0240][P 1.0227] nāma sambuddho, sayambhū aparājito;

Araññe parinibbāyi, amanussamhi kānane.

The Sambuddha named Ānanda, self-arisen and unconquered, attained Parinibbāna in the forest, in a wood uninhabited by humans.

10.

10.

“Devalokā idhāgantvā, citaṃ katvānahaṃ tadā;

Sarīraṃ tattha jhāpesiṃ, sakkārañca akāsahaṃ.

Having come here from the deva world, I then made a pyre. I caused the body to be cremated there, and I performed acts of honor.

11.

11.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ kammamakariṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons ago, when I performed that deed, I have not known a woeful state since. This is the fruit of worshipping a Buddha.

12.

12.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā citakapūjako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Citakapūjaka spoke these verses.

Citakapūjakattherassāpadānaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third Apadāna of the Elder Citakapūjaka is finished.

4. Ticampakapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ

4. The Apadāna of the Elder Ticampakapupphiya

13.

13.

“Himavantassāvidūre[T 1.0343], vikato vikano (sī. syā.) nāma pabbato;

Tassa vemajjhe vasati, samaṇo bhāvitindriyo.

Not far from the Himavanta, there is a mountain named Vikata. In its middle dwells a monk with developed faculties.

14.

14.

“Disvāna tassopasamaṃ, vippasannena cetasā;

Tīṇi campakapupphāni, gahetvāna samokiriṃ.

Seeing his tranquility, with a very serene mind, I took three campaka flowers and scattered them.

15.

15.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhipūjayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons ago, when I offered that flower, I have not known a woeful state since. This is the fruit of worshipping a Buddha.

16.

16.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā ticampakapupphiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Ticampakapupphiya spoke these verses.

Ticampakapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth Apadāna of the Elder Ticampakapupphiya is finished.

5. Sattapāṭaliyattheraapadānaṃ

5. The Apadāna of the Elder Sattapāṭaliya

17.

17.

“Kaṇikāraṃva jotantaṃ, nisinnaṃ pabbatantare;

Satta pāṭalipupphāni, buddhassa abhiropayiṃ.

To the Buddha, shining like a kaṇikāra flower and seated in a mountain cleft, I offered seven pāṭali flowers.

18.

18.

“Catunnavutito [M 1.0257][V 1.0241] kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhiropayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-four aeons ago, when I offered that flower, I have not known a woeful state since. This is the fruit of worshipping a Buddha.

19.

19.

“Paṭisambhidā [T 1.0344] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā sattapāṭaliyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Sattapāṭaliya spoke these verses.

Sattapāṭaliyattherassāpadānaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The fifth Apadāna of the Elder Sattapāṭaliya is finished.

6. Upāhanadāyakattheraapadānaṃ

6. The Apadāna of the Elder Upāhanadāyaka

20.

20.

“Ahosiṃ [P 1.0228] candano nāma, sambuddhassatrajo tadā;

Ekopāhano mayā dinno, bodhiṃ sampajja me tuvaṃ.

I was then one named Candana, a true-born son of the Sambuddha. A pair of sandals was given by me, with the aspiration: 'May you be for my enlightenment.'

21.

21.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ pānadhiṃ yamupāhanaṃ (sī.), yaṃ pāduṃ (syā.) dadiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, upāhanassidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons ago, when I made that aspiration, I have not known a woeful state since. This is the fruit of the sandals.

22.

22.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā upāhanadāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Upāhanadāyaka spoke these verses.

Upāhanadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The sixth Apadāna of the Elder Upāhanadāyaka is finished.

7. Mañjaripūjakattheraapadānaṃ

7. The Apadāna of the Elder Mañjaripūjaka

23.

23.

“Mañjarikaṃ karitvāna, rathiyaṃ paṭipajjahaṃ;

Addasaṃ samaṇānaggaṃ, bhikkhusaṅghapurakkhataṃ.

Having made a flower cluster, I proceeded along the road; I saw the foremost of ascetics, attended by the community of monks.

24.

24.

“Pasannacitto [T 1.0345] sumano, paramāya ca pītiyā;

Ubho hatthehi paggayha, buddhassa abhiropayiṃ.

With a serene and gladdened mind, and with supreme joy, having raised it with both hands, I offered it to the Buddha.

25.

25.

“Dvenavute ito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhipūjayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, pupphapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-two aeons ago, when I worshipped with that flower, I have not known a woeful state since. This is the fruit of offering a flower.

26.

26.

“Ito [M 1.0258] tesattatikappe, eko āsiṃ mahīpati;

Jotiyo nāma nāmena, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Seventy-three aeons ago from this one, I was once a ruler of the earth, a wheel-turning monarch of great power, by the name of Jotiyo.

27.

27.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā mañjaripūjako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the venerable elder Mañjaripūjaka spoke these verses.

Mañjaripūjakattherassāpadānaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh Apadāna of the Elder Mañjaripūjaka is finished.

8. Paṇṇadāyakattheraapadānaṃ

8. The Apadāna of the Elder Paṇṇadāyaka

28.

28.

“Pabbate [V 1.0242] himavantamhi, vākacīradharo ahaṃ;

Aloṇapaṇṇabhakkhomhi, niyamesu ca saṃvuto.

On the Himālaya mountain, I was a wearer of bark-cloth; I ate unsalted leaves, and I was well-restrained in my observances.

29.

29.

“Pātarāse anuppatte, siddhattho upagacchi maṃ;

Tāhaṃ buddhassa pādāsiṃ, pasanno sehi pāṇibhi.

When the time for the morning meal arrived, Siddhattha approached me. With a serene mind, I gave it to the Buddha with my own hands.

30.

30.

“Catunnavutito [P 1.0229] kappe, yaṃ paṇṇamadadiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, paṇṇadānassidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-four aeons from now, when I gave that leaf, I have known no woeful state since; this is the fruit of the gift of a leaf.

31.

31.

“Sattavīsatikappamhi[T 1.0346], rājā āsiṃ sadatthiyo yadatthiyo (sī. syā.);

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

In the twenty-seventh aeon from now, I was a king named Sadatthiyo, endowed with the seven treasures, a wheel-turning monarch of great power.

32.

32.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, these eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā paṇṇadāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the venerable elder Paṇṇadāyaka spoke these verses.

Paṇṇadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The eighth Apadāna of the Elder Paṇṇadāyaka.

9. Kuṭidāyakattheraapadānaṃ

9. The Apadāna of the Elder Kuṭidāyaka

33.

33.

“Vipinacārī sambuddho, rukkhamūle vasī tadā;

Paṇṇasālaṃ karitvāna, adāsiṃ aparājite.

The Fully Enlightened One, a wanderer in the forest, was at that time dwelling at the foot of a tree. Having made a leaf-hut, I gave it to the Unconquered One.

34.

34.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ paṇṇakuṭikaṃ adaṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, kuṭidānassidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons from now, when I gave that leaf-hut, I have known no woeful state since; this is the fruit of the gift of a hut.

35.

35.

“Aṭṭhavīse [M 1.0259] aṭṭhatiṃse (syā.) ito kappe, soḷasāsiṃsu rājāno;

Sabbattha abhivassīti, vuccare cakkavattino.

Twenty-eight aeons from now, I was a king sixteen times. They are called wheel-turning monarchs because they hold sway everywhere.

36.

36.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, these eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā kuṭidāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the venerable elder Kuṭidāyaka spoke these verses.

Kuṭidāyakattherassāpadānaṃ navamaṃ.

The ninth Apadāna of the Elder Kuṭidāyaka.

10. Aggapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ

10. The Apadāna of the Elder Aggapupphiya

37.

37.

“Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ [T 1.0347][V 1.0243] sambuddhaṃ, nisinnaṃ pabbatantare;

Obhāsayantaṃ raṃsena raṃsiyā (syā.), sikhinaṃ sikhinaṃ yathā.

I saw the Fully Enlightened One, Sikhī, of golden complexion, seated in a mountain cleft, illuminating with his rays, like a blazing fire.

38.

38.

“Aggajaṃ pupphamādāya, upāgacchiṃ naruttamaṃ;

Pasannacitto sumano, buddhassa abhiropayiṃ.

Taking the most excellent flower, I approached the highest of men. With a serene and joyful mind, I offered it to the Buddha.

39.

39.

“Ekattiṃse ito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhipūjayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Thirty-one aeons from now, when I worshipped with that flower, I have known no woeful state since; this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.

40.

40.

“Pañcavīsatikappamhi, ahosi amitogato amitavhayo (sī.);

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

In the twenty-fifth aeon, I was a wheel-turning monarch named Amitogata, endowed with the seven treasures and of great power.

41.

41.

“Paṭisambhidā [P 1.0230] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, these eight liberations, and the six direct knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā aggapupphiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the venerable elder Aggapupphiya spoke these verses.

Aggapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth Apadāna of the Elder Aggapupphiya.

Thomakavaggo chabbīsatimo.

The twenty-sixth chapter, the Thomaka Vagga.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Thomakekāsanacitakaṃ, campako sattapāṭali;

Pānadhi [T 1.0348] pāhano (sī.), pādu (syā.) mañjarī paṇṇaṃ, kuṭido aggapupphiyo;

Gāthāyo gaṇitā cettha, ekatālīsameva cāti.

Thomaka, Ekāsana, Citaka, Campaka, Sattapāṭali, Pānadhi, Mañjarī, Paṇṇa, Kuṭida, and Aggapupphiya. And here the verses are counted as forty-one.

27. Padumukkhipavaggo

The Padumukkhipa Vagga

1. Ākāsukkhipiyattheraapadānaṃ

The Apadāna of the Elder Ākāsukkhipiya

1.

1.

“Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ [M 1.0260][V 1.0244] siddhatthaṃ, gacchantaṃ antarāpaṇe;

Jalajagge duve gayha, upāgacchiṃ narāsabhaṃ.

27. I saw the Buddha Siddhattha, of golden complexion, walking in the market street. Taking two of the finest lotuses, I approached the bull among men.

2.

2.

“Ekañca pupphaṃ pādesu, buddhaseṭṭhassa nikkhipiṃ;

Ekañca pupphaṃ paggayha, ākāse ukkhipiṃ ahaṃ.

1. One flower I placed at the feet of the best of Buddhas, and one flower, having raised it up, I tossed into the sky.

3.

3.

“Catunnavutito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhiropayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, pupphadānassidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-four aeons from now, when I offered that flower, I have known no woeful state since; this is the fruit of the gift of a flower.

4.

4.

“Ito chattiṃsakappamhi, eko āsiṃ mahīpati;

Antalikkhakaro nāma, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Thirty-six aeons from now, I was a king, a ruler of the earth, named Antalikkhakara, a wheel-turning monarch of great power.

5.

5.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso, vimokkhāpi ca aṭṭhime;

Chaḷabhiññā sacchikatā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, these eight liberations, and the six direct knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā ākāsukkhipiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the venerable elder Ākāsukkhipiya spoke these verses.

Ākāsukkhipiyattherassāpadānaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first Apadāna of the Elder Ākāsukkhipiya.

2. Telamakkhiyattheraapadānaṃ

The Apadāna of the Elder Telamakkhiya

6.

6.

“Siddhatthamhi [T 1.0349] bhagavati, nibbutamhi narāsabhe;

Bodhiyā vedikāyāhaṃ, telaṃ makkhesi tāvade.

When the Blessed One Siddhattha, the bull among men, had attained Parinibbāna, I at that very moment anointed the railing of the Bodhi tree with oil.

7.

7.

“Catunnavutito [P 1.0231] kappe, yaṃ telaṃ makkhayiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, makkhanāya idaṃ phalaṃ.

2. Ninety-four aeons from now, when I anointed with that oil, I have known no woeful state since; this is the fruit of that anointing.

8.

8.

“Catuvīse ito kappe, succhavi nāma khattiyo;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Twenty-four aeons from now, I was a khattiya named Succhavi, endowed with the seven treasures, a wheel-turning monarch of great power.

9.

9.

“Paṭisambhidā [V 1.0245] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, these eight liberations, and the six direct knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā telamakkhiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the venerable elder Telamakkhiya spoke these verses.

Telamakkhiyattherassāpadānaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second Apadāna of the Elder Telamakkhiya.

3. Aḍḍhacandiyattheraapadānaṃ

The Apadāna of the Elder Aḍḍhacandiya

10.

10.

“Tissassa [M 1.0261] kho bhagavato, bodhiyā pādaputtame;

Aḍḍhacandaṃ mayā dinnaṃ, dharaṇīruhapādape.

To the Bodhi tree of the Blessed One Tissa, the most excellent of trees, a tree that grows upon the earth, I gave an offering in the shape of a half-moon.

11.

11.

“Dvenavute ito kappe, yaṃ canda yaṃ puppha (ka.) mabhiropayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, bodhipūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-two aeons from this world cycle, when I offered that half-moon shape, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of venerating the Bodhi tree.

12.

12.

“Pañcavīse [T 1.0350] ito kappe, devalo nāma khattiyo;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Twenty-five aeons from this world cycle, I was a khattiya named Devala, a wheel-turning monarch endowed with the seven treasures and of great strength.

13.

13.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā aḍḍhacandiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the Venerable Elder Aḍḍhacandiya spoke these verses.

Aḍḍhacandiyattherassāpadānaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third apadāna, of the Elder Aḍḍhacandiya, is concluded.

4. Padīpadāyakattheraapadānaṃ

4. The Apadāna of the Elder Padīpadāyaka

14.

14.

“Devabhūto ahaṃ santo, oruyha pathaviṃ tadā;

Padīpe pañca pādāsiṃ, pasanno sehi pāṇibhi.

Then, being a deva, I descended to the earth. With a serene mind, I offered five lamps with my own hands.

15.

15.

“Catunnavutito kappe, yaṃ padīpamadaṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, dīpadānassidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-four aeons from this world cycle, when I gave that lamp, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of the gift of a lamp.

16.

16.

“Pañcapaññāsake kappe, eko āsiṃ mahīpati;

Samantacakkhunāmena, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

In the fifty-fifth aeon, I was once a ruler of the earth named Samantacakkhu, a wheel-turning monarch of great strength.

17.

17.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā padīpadāyako apaṇṇadīpiyo (sī. ka.) thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the Venerable Elder Padīpadāyaka spoke these verses.

Padīpadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth apadāna, of the Elder Padīpadāyaka, is concluded.

5. Biḷālidāyakattheraapadānaṃ

5. The Apadāna of the Elder Biḷālidāyaka

18.

18.

“Himavantassāvidūre[T 1.0351][V 1.0246][P 1.0232], romaso nāma pabbato;

Tamhi pabbatapādamhi, samaṇo bhāvitindriyo.

Not far from the Himālaya, there is a mountain named Romasa. At the foot of that mountain dwells an ascetic with developed faculties.

19.

19.

“Biḷāliyo [M 1.0262] gahetvāna, samaṇassa adāsahaṃ;

Anumodi mahāvīro, sayambhū aparājito.

Taking taro roots, I gave them to the ascetic. The Great Hero, the Self-Awakened, the Unconquered One, rejoiced in my merit.

20.

20.

“Biḷālī te mama dinnā, vippasannena cetasā;

Bhave nibbattamānamhi, phalaṃ nibbattataṃ tava.

‘You gave me these taro roots with a very serene mind. As you arise in future existences, may the fruit thereof manifest for you.’

21.

21.

“Catunnavutito kappe, yaṃ biḷālimadāsahaṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, biḷāliyā idaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-four aeons from this world cycle, when I gave that taro root, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of that taro root offering.

22.

22.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā biḷālidāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the Venerable Elder Biḷālidāyaka spoke these verses.

Biḷālidāyakattherassāpadānaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The fifth apadāna, of the Elder Biḷālidāyaka, is concluded.

6. Macchadāyakattheraapadānaṃ

6. The Apadāna of the Elder Macchadāyaka

23.

23.

“Candabhāgānadītīre, ukkuso āsahaṃ tadā;

Mahantaṃ macchaṃ paggayha, siddhatthamunino adaṃ.

On the bank of the Candabhāgā River, I was an osprey at that time. Seizing a great fish, I offered it to the sage Siddhattha.

24.

24.

“Catunnavutito [T 1.0352] kappe, yaṃ macchamadadiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, macchadānassidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-four aeons from this world cycle, when I gave that fish, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of the gift of a fish.

25.

25.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā macchadāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the Venerable Elder Macchadāyaka spoke these verses.

Macchadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The sixth apadāna, of the Elder Macchadāyaka, is concluded.

7. Javahaṃsakattheraapadānaṃ

7. The Apadāna of the Elder Javahaṃsaka

26.

26.

“Candabhāgānadītīre, āsiṃ vanacaro tadā;

Siddhatthaṃ addasaṃ buddhaṃ, gacchantaṃ anilañjase.

On the bank of the Candabhāgā River, I was a forest-dweller then. I saw the Buddha Siddhattha traveling through the sky.

27.

27.

“Añjaliṃ [V 1.0247] paggahetvāna, ullokento mahāmuniṃ;

Sakaṃ cittaṃ pasādetvā, avandiṃ nāyakaṃ ahaṃ.

Having raised my hands in reverence, looking up at the Great Sage, and making my own mind serene, I paid homage to the Leader.

28.

28.

“Catunnavutito [M 1.0263][P 1.0233] kappe, yamavandiṃ narāsabhaṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, vandanāya idaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-four aeons from this world cycle, when I paid homage to that Bull among Men, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of that veneration.

29.

29.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā javahaṃsako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the Venerable Elder Javahaṃsaka spoke these verses.

Javahaṃsakattherassāpadānaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh apadāna, of the Elder Javahaṃsaka, is concluded.

8. Saḷalapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ

8. The Apadāna of the Elder Saḷalapupphiya

30.

30.

“Candabhāgānadītīre[T 1.0353], ahosiṃ kinnaro tadā;

Vipassiṃ addasaṃ buddhaṃ, raṃsijālasamākulaṃ.

On the bank of the Candabhāgā River, I was a kinnara then. I saw the Buddha Vipassī, suffused with a net of rays.

31.

31.

“Pasannacitto sumano, paramāya ca pītiyā;

Paggayha saḷalaṃ pupphaṃ, vipassiṃ okiriṃ ahaṃ.

With a serene and joyful mind, and with supreme delight, I took a pine flower and scattered it over the Buddha Vipassī.

32.

32.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ pupphamabhipūjayiṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, buddhapūjāyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons from this world cycle, when I venerated him with that flower, I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of venerating the Buddha.

33.

33.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, the eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā saḷalapupphiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, indeed, the Venerable Elder Saḷalapupphiya spoke these verses.

Saḷalapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Eighth Apadāna of the Elder Saḷalapupphiya is concluded.

9. Upāgatāsayattheraapadānaṃ

9. The Apadāna of the Elder Upāgatāsaya.

34.

34.

“Himavantassa vemajjhe, saro āsi sunimmito;

Tatthāhaṃ rakkhaso āsiṃ, heṭhasīlo bhayānako.

In the middle of the Himavanta, there was a well-created lake. There I was a terrifying rakkhasa of a cruel nature.

35.

35.

“Anukampako kāruṇiko, vipassī lokanāyako;

Mamuddharitukāmo so, āgacchi mama santikaṃ.

Compassionate, merciful, the world's leader, Vipassī, wishing to lift me up, came into my presence.

36.

36.

“Upāgataṃ [T 1.0354] mahāvīraṃ, devadevaṃ narāsabhaṃ;

Āsayā abhinikkhamma, avandiṃ satthuno ahaṃ.

Having emerged from my abode, I paid homage to the Teacher, the Great Hero who had approached, the god beyond gods, the Leader of men.

37.

37.

“Ekanavutito [M 1.0264][V 1.0248] kappe, yaṃ vandiṃ purisuttamaṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, vandanāya idaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons from this one, I paid homage to that supreme person. Since then, I have not known a woeful state; this is the fruit of paying homage.

38.

38.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been done.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā upāgatāsayo upāgatahāsaniyo (syā.), upāgatāhāsaniyo (ka.) thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Upāgatāsaya spoke these verses.

Upāgatāsayattherassāpadānaṃ navamaṃ.

The Ninth Apadāna of the Elder Upāgatāsaya is concluded.

10. Taraṇiyattheraapadānaṃ

10. The Apadāna of the Elder Taraṇiya.

39.

39.

“Suvaṇṇavaṇṇo [P 1.0234] sambuddho, vipassī dakkhiṇāraho;

Nadītīre ṭhito satthā, bhikkhusaṅghapurakkhato.

The Perfectly Enlightened One, Vipassī, of golden complexion and worthy of offerings, the Teacher, surrounded by the community of bhikkhus, stood on the riverbank.

40.

40.

“Nāvā na vijjate tattha, santāraṇī mahaṇṇave;

Nadiyā abhinikkhamma, tāresiṃ lokanāyakaṃ.

There was no ferry boat there in that great river for crossing. Emerging from the river, I ferried the world-leader across.

41.

41.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yaṃ tāresiṃ naruttamaṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, taraṇāya idaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons from this one, I ferried that best of men across. Since then, I have not known a woeful state; this is the fruit of that ferrying.

42.

42.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been done.

Itthaṃ [T 1.0355] sudaṃ āyasmā taraṇiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Taraṇiya spoke these verses.

Taraṇiyattherassāpadānaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Tenth Apadāna of the Elder Taraṇiya is concluded.

Padumukkhipavaggo sattavīsatimo.

The Padumukkhipa Chapter, the twenty-seventh.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of this is:

Ukkhipī telacandī ca, dīpado ca biḷālido;

Maccho javo saḷalado, rakkhaso taraṇo dasa;

Gāthāyo cettha saṅkhātā, tālīsaṃ cekameva cāti.

Ukkhipī, Telacandī, and Dīpado, Biḷālido, Maccho, Javo, Saḷalado, Rakkhaso, Taraṇo—these ten. Here forty-one verses are enumerated.

28. Suvaṇṇabibbohanavaggo

28. The Suvaṇṇabibbohana Chapter

1. Suvaṇṇabibbohaniyattheraapadānaṃ

1. The Apadāna of the Elder Suvaṇṇabibbohaniyo

1.

1.

“Ekāsanaṃ [T 1.0356][M 1.0265][V 1.0249] ahamadaṃ, pasanno sehi pāṇibhi;

Bibbohanañca bimbohanañca (sī. pī.) pādāsiṃ, uttamatthassa pattiyā.

With faith, I gave a single seat with my own hands; and I offered a cushion for the sake of attaining the highest goal.

2.

2.

“Ekanavutito kappe, bibbohanamadāsahaṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, bibbohanassidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons from this one, I gave a cushion; since then, I have not known a woeful state. This is the fruit of offering a cushion.

3.

3.

“Ito tesaṭṭhime kappe, asamo nāma khattiyo;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Sixty-three aeons from this one, I was a khattiya named Asama, a wheel-turning monarch endowed with the seven treasures and of great power.

4.

4.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso, vimokkhāpi ca aṭṭhime;

Chaḷabhiññā sacchikatā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, these eight liberations, and the six supernormal knowledges have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā suvaṇṇabibbohaniyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Suvaṇṇabibbohaniyo spoke these verses.

Suvaṇṇabibbohaniyattherassāpadānaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The First Apadāna of the Elder Suvaṇṇabibbohaniyo is concluded.

2. Tilamuṭṭhidāyakattheraapadānaṃ

2. The Apadāna of the Elder Tilamuṭṭhidāyaka

5.

5.

“Mama [P 1.0235] saṅkappamaññāya, satthā lokagganāyako;

Manomayena kāyena, iddhiyā upasaṅkami.

Knowing my intention, the Teacher, the world’s foremost leader, approached by psychic power with a mind-made body.

6.

6.

“Satthāraṃ upasaṅkantaṃ, vanditvā purisuttamaṃ;

Pasannacitto sumano, tilamuṭṭhimadāsahaṃ.

Having paid homage to the Teacher, the supreme among men, who had approached, with a pleased and gladdened mind, I gave a handful of sesame.

7.

7.

“Ekanavutito [T 1.0357] kappe, yaṃ dānamadadiṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, tilamuṭṭhiyidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-one aeons from this one, when I gave that gift, since then I have not known a woeful state. This is the fruit of that handful of sesame.

8.

8.

“Ito soḷasakappamhi, tantiso khantiyo (syā.) nāma khattiyo;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Sixteen aeons from this one, I was a khattiya named Tantisa, a wheel-turning monarch endowed with the seven treasures and of great power.

9.

9.

“Paṭisambhidā [V 1.0250] catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā tilamuṭṭhidāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Tilamuṭṭhidāyaka spoke these verses.

Tilamuṭṭhidāyakattherassāpadānaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Second Apadāna of the Elder Tilamuṭṭhidāyaka is concluded.

3. Caṅkoṭakiyattheraapadānaṃ

3. The Apadāna of the Elder Caṅkoṭakiya

10.

10.

“Mahāsamuddaṃ [M 1.0266] nissāya, vasatī pabbatantare;

Paccuggantvāna katvāna paccuggantvāna’kāsahaṃ (aṭṭha.), paccuggamanaṃ katvāna (?), caṅkoṭaka caṅgoṭaka (sī.) madāsahaṃ.

He was dwelling among the mountains, near the great ocean. Having gone out to meet him and made a flower basket, I gave it.

11.

11.

“Siddhatthassa mahesino, sabbasattānukampino sayambhussānukampino (syā.);

Pupphacaṅkoṭakaṃ datvā, kappaṃ saggamhi modahaṃ.

Having given a flower basket to Siddhattha, the great sage, compassionate to all beings, I rejoiced in the heavenly world for an aeon.

12.

12.

“Catunnavutito kappe, caṅkoṭakamadaṃ tadā;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, caṅkoṭakassidaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-four aeons from this one, I gave a flower basket; since then, I have not known a woeful state. This is the fruit of offering a flower basket.

13.

13.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

Itthaṃ [T 1.0358] sudaṃ āyasmā caṅkoṭakiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Caṅkoṭakiyo spoke these verses.

Caṅkoṭakiyattherassāpadānaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third Apadāna of the Elder Caṅkoṭakiyo is concluded.

4. Abbhañjanadāyakattheraapadānaṃ

4. The Apadāna of the Elder Abbhañjanadāyaka

14.

14.

“Koṇḍaññassa [P 1.0236] bhagavato, vītarāgassa tādino;

Ākāsasamacittassa akakkasacittassātha (aṭṭha.), nippapañcassa jhāyino.

To the Blessed One Koṇḍañña, free from passion, steadfast, with a mind like the sky, free from proliferation, the meditator;

15.

15.

“Sabbamohātivattassa, sabbalokahitesino;

Abbhañjanaṃ mayā dinnaṃ, dvipadindassa tādino.

To him who had transcended all delusion, who sought the welfare of the entire world, to the steadfast lord of bipeds, an unguent was given by me.

16.

16.

“Aparimeyye ito kappe, abbhañjanamadaṃ tadā ambhañjanamadāsahaṃ (syā.);

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, abbhañjanassidaṃ phalaṃ.

In an incalculable aeon from this one, I gave an unguent at that time. I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of the unguent.

17.

17.

“Ito pannarase kappe, cirappo nāma khattiyo;

Sattaratanasampanno, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Fifteen aeons from now, I was a khattiya named Cirappo, endowed with the seven treasures, a wheel-turning monarch of great power.

18.

18.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges... the teaching of the Buddha has been done.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā abbhañjanadāyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the venerable Elder Abbhañjanadāyaka spoke these verses.

Abbhañjanadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth Apadāna of the Elder Abbhañjanadāyaka is concluded.

5. Ekañjalikattheraapadānaṃ

5. The Apadāna of the Elder Ekañjalika

19.

19.

“Udumbare [T 1.0359][M 1.0267][V 1.0251] vasantassa, niyate paṇṇasanthare;

Vutthokāso mayā dinno, samaṇassa mahesino.

To the great sage, the ascetic, dwelling at an Udumbara tree on a permanent spread of leaves, a dwelling place was given by me.

20.

20.

“Tissassa dvipadindassa, lokanāthassa tādino;

Añjaliṃ paggahetvāna, santhariṃ pupphasantharaṃ.

Having raised my joined hands in reverence, I spread a covering of flowers for Tissa, the lord of bipeds, the protector of the world, the steadfast one.

21.

21.

“Dvenavute ito kappe, yaṃ kariṃ pupphasantharaṃ;

Duggatiṃ nābhijānāmi, santharassa idaṃ phalaṃ.

Ninety-two aeons from now, I made that flower-covering. I have known no woeful state; this is the fruit of that covering.

22.

22.

“Ito cuddasakappamhi, ahosiṃ manujādhipo;

Ekaañjaliko nāma, cakkavattī mahabbalo.

Fourteen aeons from now, I was a ruler of men named Ekañjalika, a wheel-turning monarch of great power.

23.

24.

24.

31.

32.

36.

38.

38.

39.

“Ekanavutito kappe, yo setu kārito mayā;

40.

41.

“Paṭisambhidā catasso…pe… kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ”.

The four analytical knowledges, these eight liberations, and the six supernormal powers have been realized. The teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.
